quote: Theorem. Let X1 and X2 be two independent random variables following the GTL−HT−G family of distributions with common parameters θ, b, ψ, and different shape parameters δ1 and δ2, that is, X1 ∼ f1(x; δ1, θ, b, ψ) and X2 ∼ f2(x; δ2, θ, b, ψ). If δ1 > δ2, then X1 and X2 are stochastically ordered.
family: Gamma Topp-Leone-Heavy-Tailed-G (GTL−HT−G) family, cdf F(x; δ, b, θ, ψ) = 1 − γ(−log(1 − U_G(x; θ, ψ))^b, δ)/Γ(δ) with U_G(x; θ, ψ) = [G(x, ψ)/(1 − (1 − θ)G(x, ψ))]^{2θ}, parameters δ, b, θ > 0 and baseline parameter vector ψ
compared: shape parameter δ1 vs δ2; common θ, b, ψ

hypotheses.text: Let X1 and X2 be two independent random variables following the GTL−HT−G family of distributions with common parameters θ, b, ψ, and different shape parameters δ1 and δ2
hypotheses.formal: X1 ~ GTL-HT-G(δ1, θ, b, ψ), X2 ~ GTL-HT-G(δ2, θ, b, ψ), independent

hypotheses.text: for δ, b, θ > 0 and parameter vector ψ

conclusion.direction: f1/f2 non-increasing in x, i.e. X1 <=lr X2 (statement only says 'stochastically ordered'; proof derives lr order, which implies hr and st order per the section's implication X ⪯lr Y => X ⪯hr Y => X ⪯ Y)

quantifiers: δ1 > δ2, θ, b > 0, all x in the support
ambiguity: The theorem is unnumbered and states only 'stochastically ordered' without a direction. The proof writes 'likelihood ratio order X ⪯lr Y exists' using undefined X, Y (the preamble defines X1, X2). The likelihood-ratio denominator is printed as f2(x; δ1, θ, b, ψ) — an apparent typo for δ2 — in equation (11) and again in its derivative. Independence of X1, X2 is irrelevant to the marginal ordering conclusion.
